oneLiner: Peak-cycle memory printing 87% gross margins on an AI-driven DRAM/HBM/NAND shortage, guiding to a record $61.5B quarter yet trading near $1,100 at roughly 7x annualized forward earnings.
thesis: One of three companies able to make leading-edge DRAM at scale; HBM revenue grew faster than total revenue in Q4 FY2026, and Micron is working with NVIDIA on the first custom HBM4E (NV-HBM).

Contracts are turning cyclical pricing into backlog: 26 strategic customer agreements (SCAs) estimated at over 35% of revenue through 2030, ~$150B of remaining performance obligations, $32B of customer financial commitments (mostly cash deposits), and more than 75% of FY2027 output already committed (all per Q4 FY2026 call).

Q4 FY2026 revenue $54.23B (vs $11.32B a year earlier) at 86.8% GAAP gross margin and $33.2B of quarterly adjusted free cash flow; FY2026 revenue $133.19B and adjusted FCF $62.3B: earnings power without precedent in memory history.

The whole question is durability: management says supply will be tighter in FY2027-28 than in 2026 and guides sequential revenue growth every quarter of FY2027, but price increases are moderating and FY2027 capex is stepping up sharply (1H ~$25B, 2H higher).

latestQuarter.label: Q4 FY2026 (ended Sep 3, 2026; reported Sep 30, 2026)
points: Revenue $54.23B, +379% YoY, +31% QoQ; GAAP gross margin 86.8% (non-GAAP 87.0%); GAAP operating margin 80.7% (non-GAAP 82.3%).
GAAP EPS $32.87; non-GAAP EPS $33.42 vs ~$31.6 consensus (LSEG, per press reports); GAAP net income $37.70B.
Operating cash flow $43.97B; net capex $10.77B; adjusted FCF $33.20B. Net cash $68.3B; customer deposits $12.7B on balance sheet.
DRAM $39.8B (73% of revenue, prices up high-teens % QoQ); NAND $14.1B (26%, prices up ~30% QoQ); data center SSD nearly $10B.
Guide: Q1 FY2027 revenue $61.5B +/- $1.5B, non-GAAP gross margin ~86.25%, EPS $38.15 +/- $1.00; Q1 called the FY2027 gross-margin floor.

segments: Q4 FY2026: DRAM $39.8B (73%), NAND $14.1B (26%). By business unit: core data center $18.0B (90% GM), cloud memory $16.3B (83% GM, diluted by HBM mix), mobile/client $13.1B (90% GM), auto/embedded $6.8B (84% GM). FY2026 DRAM revenue surpassed $100B.

HBM is the strategic prize: the vast majority of calendar-2027 HBM bit supply is contracted at significantly higher prices YoY, narrowing the margin gap with conventional DRAM; HBM4 ramping, custom HBM4E (NV-HBM) with NVIDIA next. Singapore HBM packaging output expected early calendar 2027.
competitive: HBM share remains contested and tracker-dependent: one Q2 2026 read puts SK Hynix at 50%, Samsung 32% and Micron 18%; another has SK hynix near 62% with Micron having passed Samsung.
Scale is the structural gap: Samsung and SK Hynix each run roughly 150,000-200,000 HBM wafers a month, three to four times Micron's base. Micron's ID1 fab outputs mid-2027, ID2 late 2028.
NAND: fifth place (~11% share) behind Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia and Sandisk, though NAND revenue grew 42% QoQ in Q4 FY2026.
CXMT (China) hit 7.6% of global DRAM in Q1 2026 and IPO'd at roughly $85B; not yet at the leading edge.
Analysts raised talk of a large customer de-speccing HBM on the Q4 call; management replied that HBM demand outgrows conventional DRAM through 2028 (customer and magnitude unverified).
moat: Leading-edge DRAM process capability (1-gamma is now its largest node), HBM4 plus a custom HBM4E program with the dominant AI platform, and take-or-pay SCAs - three quarters of SCA revenue has a defined pricing framework, mostly floor-and-ceiling bands. Breadth across HBM, LPDDR/SOCAMM, DDR5 and data center SSD lets wafers chase the highest return. The binding limit is clean-room capacity, not demand.
risks: Peak-cycle earnings: 87% gross margins are unprecedented and mean-reverting; management guides a more moderate rate of price increases in FY2027, and Morningstar cut its fair value citing faster-than-expected pricing deceleration.
Capex step-up: 1H FY2027 net capex ~$25B with 2H higher (analysts infer more than $50B for the year), weighted to construction - raising fixed costs and depreciation if pricing softens.
Beat magnitude narrowing: Q4 non-GAAP EPS beat ~5-7% versus 20%+ earlier in the cycle; FY2027 opex guided up ~$2.5B.
Capacity race: Samsung and SK Hynix add supply from a base three to four times larger; CXMT share gains (7.6% and rising).
HBM content risk if a large customer de-specs memory per accelerator (reported, unverified), which could also release wafers back to conventional DRAM.
NAND structurally smaller at ~11% share despite the current price surge.
catalysts: Increased capital return beginning Dec 9, 2026 (management intends to return 100% of excess cash over time); $0.15 quarterly dividend payable Oct 29, 2026.
Q1 FY2027 earnings in late December 2026 (date unverified; guide $61.5B revenue, ~86.25% gross margin, $38.15 EPS) - first test of the 'Q1 is the margin floor' claim.
Calendar-2027 HBM price step-up taking effect from January 2027; HBM4 multi-customer ramp and NV-HBM (custom HBM4E) milestones.
Further SCA signings and 2028 supply negotiations (already under way per management).
TrendForce Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 contract-price prints, plus CXMT capacity news flow.
pricedIn: The stock closed at $1,097.39 on Oct 1, 2026, up 3.0% the day after the Q4 print, still about 10% below the $1,213.37 all-time closing high of Jun 25. Annualizing the Q1 FY2027 EPS guide ($38.15 x 4 = ~$153) gives roughly 7.2x forward earnings, and ~14.5x FY2026 non-GAAP EPS of $75.52 (both derived). Debate: a single-digit multiple on peak EPS is exactly what a cycle top looks like, and a $50B-plus capex year plus moderating price increases give the bears their entry - against which sit ~$150B of RPO, 75%+ of FY2027 output committed, and $32B of customer commitments that make this cycle more durable than any before it.

scenarios.bear: FY2027 marks the peak: price increases fade as new capacity lands in 2027-28, the capex surge becomes stranded depreciation, CXMT floods conventional DRAM, margins compress toward the 50s, SCA floors bind, EPS halves, and the stock de-rates the way every prior memory cycle ended.
scenarios.base: FY2027 is another record with sequential growth each quarter as guided; Q1 at ~86% gross margin proves the floor, calendar-2027 HBM is pre-sold at higher prices, and SCA floors cushion any conventional slowdown; earnings plateau high rather than collapse, with violent cycle-headline volatility.
scenarios.bull: Supply stays tight through 2028 as management claims; HBM pricing converges toward conventional DRAM margins, NV-HBM wins share, NAND scarcity extends, capital return to 100% of excess cash lands, and the ~7x multiple re-rates toward 10x as the market accepts a structurally higher earnings floor.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: at roughly 7x annualized forward EPS (Oct 2026) the market is still pricing a memory downcycle, and the reverse DCF quantifies the implied annual earnings decline. Bear equals a deep downcycle (prior cycles saw EPS halve or worse); bull is the structural-shortage case where earnings hold and grow.

latestProse: Q4 FY2026 (ended Sep 3; reported Sep 30). Revenue $54.23B versus $11.32B a year earlier (+379%) and above the $50B +/- $1B guide; GAAP gross margin 86.8%, GAAP operating margin 80.7% (operating income $43.75B). Non-GAAP EPS $33.42 against ~$31.6 consensus; GAAP net income $37.70B ($32.87 per share). Operating cash flow was $43.97B and adjusted free cash flow $33.20B after $10.77B of net capex. DRAM was a record $39.8B (73% of revenue) on high-teens price increases; NAND $14.1B (26%) on ~30% price increases, with data center SSD nearly $10B. FY2026 revenue $133.19B, non-GAAP EPS $75.52. The disclosure that matters most: 26 take-or-pay SCAs now underpin ~$150B of remaining performance obligations and $32B of customer financial commitments, with more than 75% of FY2027 output committed - the contractual floor is the entire argument against valuing this as a normal cycle top.
guidanceProse: Q1 FY2027 guide: revenue $61.5B +/- $1.5B, non-GAAP gross margin ~86.25% (GAAP ~85.95%), opex ~$2.06B, non-GAAP EPS $38.15 +/- $1.00 on ~1.15B shares - roughly 8% above consensus. Management calls Q1 the gross-margin floor for FY2027 (higher incentive compensation lands in Q1), expects higher margins thereafter with a more moderate rate of price increases, sequential revenue growth every quarter, FY2027 opex up ~$2.5B and a ~15.5% tax rate. Net capex ~$11.5B in Q1 and ~$25B in 1H FY2027, higher in 2H and weighted to construction for clean-room space from late 2028. The market pays roughly 7x annualized forward earnings for the combination.
